Comparison

Platform Architecture Comparison

A technical breakdown of how the Olympus dashboard was architected in each platform.

Dimension CRM Analytics (Before) Tableau Next (After)
Data Layer Flat dataset snapshot (OlympusOpportunities_DataCloud_csv) ✓ Live Data Cloud DLO — Opportunity_Home__dll
Query Engine SAQL (Salesforce-proprietary) ✓ VizQL — Tableau's visual query language
Semantic Layer None — fields used directly from dataset ✓ Semantic Model (New_Semantic_Model_9fc2) defines all exposed fields
Field Names Match SOQL exactly (Amount, StageName) Org-wide suffixed names (Amount2, Stage2, Close_Date3)
Dashboard Structure Single JSON file — all widgets inline ✓ Separate .xml file per visualization + dashboard XML
Chart Config Human-readable JSON in dashboard file Base64-encoded visualSpecification blob per viz
Filters selectMode: single/multi dropdowns viewType: toggle (comboBox avoided — runtime risk)
Layout Grid 48-column grid with row/col positions 48-column grid — same system, different XML schema
Dark Theme Native dark theme config backgroundColor: #03234D applied per widget and page style
Workspace/App CRM Analytics App ✓ AnalyticsWorkspace with workspaceAssetRelationships
Data Scale CRM-scale (dataset snapshots) ✓ Enterprise scale — billions of rows in Data Cloud
Real-time Data Scheduled dataflow refreshes ✓ Streaming ingestion via Data Cloud
AI / Insights Einstein Discovery ✓ Tableau Pulse + Einstein Copilot

Achievements

What This Migration Unlocks

☁️

Live Data Cloud Foundation

All opportunity data now flows through Salesforce Data Cloud (Opportunity_Home__dll DLO) — enabling real-time updates and multi-source data unification.

🧠

Semantic Model Layer

The Semantic Model (New_Semantic_Model_9fc2) acts as a governed, reusable data layer — any future dashboard can reference the same SM without re-ingesting data.

📈

Enterprise Scale

Tableau Next + Data Cloud supports billions of rows and real-time streaming ingestion — far beyond CRM Analytics dataset snapshot limits.

🤖

AI-Ready Platform

Tableau Pulse and Einstein Copilot can now surface AI-generated insights, anomaly detection, and natural language analytics on the same Opportunity data.

🔗

Multi-Source Unification

Data Cloud can now join Opportunity data with Marketing Cloud, Commerce Cloud, and third-party sources — creating a true 360° customer view.

🎨

Tableau VizQL Engine

All charts now run on Tableau's world-class VizQL engine — enabling LOD calculations, advanced forecasting, and richer interactive experiences than SAQL allowed.

Technical Journey

How This Migration Was Built

A step-by-step account of the Olympus migration — including the UI work, automation work, and key discoveries made along the way.

1
Halo / Claude Code

Audit CRM Analytics Dashboard

Halo retrieved the Olympus CRM Analytics app metadata via SFDX, parsed the dashboard JSON, extracted all widget types (KPI, donut ×2, horizontal bar, filters, table), field names, and aggregations. SOQL queries confirmed live Opportunity data from the connected org — 124.2M in Revenue YTD across all stages.

2
UI — Manual

Data Cloud DLO Setup

The Opportunity_Home__dll Data Lake Object was set up in Salesforce Data Cloud via the UI — connecting the Salesforce CRM connector and mapping the Opportunity object fields into the DLO. This step remains fully UI-based as Data Cloud ingestion is not yet available via REST API.

3
UI — Manual

Semantic Model Creation

The Semantic Model (New_Semantic_Model_9fc2) was created manually in the Tableau Next UI: Workspace → New → Semantic Model. Fields were added and configured — Amount, Name, CloseDate, StageName, Type, Owner.Name. Key discovery: the SM assigns org-wide suffix counters to every field — the exact suffixed names (Amount2, Name2, Close_Date3, Stage2, Type1, Owner_Name2) were confirmed via the deploy-and-fail technique.

4
UI — Manual

Visualization Creation

Each visualization — Revenue KPI, Opportunity Type Mix donut, Account Type Mix donut, Top Opportunities horizontal bar, and Details table — was created manually in the Tableau Next UI, connected to the confirmed SM field names. Individual viz files were each wired to the correct SM and workspace.

5
Halo + Manual

SM Field Name Discovery

Halo ran the deploy-and-fail loop to confirm exact SM field names — deploying test viz XML with guessed field names, reading the error ("F1 isn't a valid field in the semantic model"), incrementing the suffix, and redeploying until confirmed. All 6 field names were verified and documented in the field mapping table above.

6
UI — Manual

Dashboard Assembly

The final Olympus Opportunities dashboard was assembled in the Tableau Next UI — placing all visualizations on the 48-column grid, configuring filters (Owner, Close Date), applying the dark navy theme (#03234D), and wiring filter interactions. The dashboard was validated visually in the browser.

7
Halo / Claude Code

Git, Documentation & PR

Halo committed all migration artifacts (XML files, field mapping docs, migration guides, this report) to the feature branch, created the pull request with a full summary, and generated all documentation — including the CRM Analytics vs Tableau Next comparison, step-by-step migration guide, and the Halo automation breakdown.

Lessons Learned

Key Technical Insights

Critical knowledge gained from this migration — essential for any future CRM Analytics → Tableau Next project.

🔒

SM References Are Immutable

Once a viz is first deployed against a Semantic Model, the platform permanently locks it to that SM. Deploying the same API name with a different SM causes a silent reversion. Always use brand-new API names when changing the SM.

🚫

No XML Comments in Dashboard XML

XML comments inside <pages> or <widgets> cause a runtime "We couldn't find the Dashboard" error — even though SFDX deploy reports Succeeded. Remove all comments from dashboard XML before deploying.

🔢

Field Names Have Global Counters

SM field names carry org-wide suffix counters — the same field in a second SM gets a different suffix than in the first SM. You cannot predict these; you must discover them via deploy-and-fail or UI inspection.

🏢

Cross-Workspace SM Restriction

A viz cannot use an SM from a different workspace at runtime — even if the deploy succeeds. The generic "couldn't find the Dashboard" error is the symptom. Always verify the workspace of both the viz and the SM.

🔁

Deploy-and-Fail Loop Works

Since SM field names can't be retrieved via API or SFDX, the deploy-and-fail loop is the reliable alternative. Halo can automate this entirely — deploy, read error, fix field name, redeploy — until all fields are confirmed.

🎛️

Use toggle Not comboBox for Filters

The comboBox filter viewType may cause runtime failures when deployed via metadata. The toggle viewType is safe and reliable. Date filters may show raw ISO timestamps in some configurations — validate in browser.
